name: slide-1-opening-title
text:
From a Physical Target
to a Checkable Root

name: slide-1-question
text: Which launch angle makes the range equal to 35 m?
textPreview: Which launch angle makes the range equal to 35 m?

text:
Open by asking students to name the physical quantity that is unknown before they name a numerical method.

name: slide-2-subtitle
text: Model range minus target range becomes a quantity a solver can drive to zero
textPreview: Model range minus target range becomes a quantity a solver can drive to zero

alt: Projectile range model, target condition, and residual definition

text:
Emphasise that the residual is not a new physical law. It is the model prediction compared with the target, expressed in metres.

title: Bisection keeps a sign change alive

name: slide-5-title
text: Bisection keeps a sign change alive
textPreview: Bisection keeps a sign change alive

name: slide-5-subtitle
text: Bracket first, test the midpoint, keep the half that still straddles zero
textPreview: Bracket first, test the midpoint, keep the half that still straddles zero

name: slide-5-question
text: Why is the midpoint not enough?
textPreview: Why is the midpoint not enough?

name: slide-5-answer
text: Because bisection needs a bracket whose endpoint residuals have opposite signs.
textPreview: Because bisection needs a bracket whose endpoint residuals have opposite signs.

text:
Pause after the midpoint. Students should explain why the midpoint value alone is not enough; the endpoint sign change is the invariant.

text: The bracket width halves; the sign change is the invariant
textPreview: The bracket width halves; the sign change is the invariant

text:

name: slide-7-code
textPreview: mid_deg = (left_deg + right_deg)/2; | f_mid_m = (v0_mps^2/g_mps2)*sind(2*mid_deg) - target_m; | if abs(f_mid_m) < tolerance_m |     break...

text:
Point to each line in the scaffold and ask which physical decision it represents. The code is short because the algorithm is explicit.

text: The root is useful because substitution returns the target range
textPreview: The root is useful because substitution returns the target range

alt: Validated bisection root, direct range, and residual

text:
The stopping rule is one residual test. Then substitute the angle back into the original model so the result has physical meaning.
